title: Dispatch: contract-review corrections - roster, relevance, real absence proof (attempt 5)
description:
Human contract-based fresh full review of PR #477 at dee8d0a returned 'request
changes' with six findings. The supervisor independently confirmed all six and
found a seventh. The reviewer states this is the FIRST valid transitional
checkpoint, so one correction round is permitted; the rescope/decomposition stop
rule does not apply yet. Do not squander it.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.md
  packages/core/src/rules/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts

=== READ THIS FIRST — THE PATTERN BEHIND FINDINGS 2 AND 3 ===
Both are the same failure: a required field was filled MECHANICALLY to satisfy a
validator rather than carrying real evidence. The sibling PR #476 failed twice
for exactly this and had to be decomposed. Do not fill any field this round with
a value derived from the row's own name or position. If real evidence does not
exist for a row, the row must SAY SO in a machine-checkable way and block
closure — never synthesize a plausible-looking value.

=== F1: THE 31-ROW MEMBERSHIP IS NOT PROTECTED ===
The validator enforces uniqueness, all ten families, >=2 primitives per family
and the seven non-pack rows — but never compares the ledger against the complete
primitive set. A readiness-backed row can be deleted from a 3- or 4-row family
and every test still passes.
FIX: commit a canonical, versioned primitive ROSTER (capabilityId + primitive)
and have the validator assert the ledger's set equals it exactly — missing and
unexpected both fail. Adding a primitive must require deliberately editing the
roster. Test both directions.

=== F2: AUDIT FINDINGS ARE 'RESOLVED' BY ALIAS EXISTENCE, NOT RELEVANCE ===
CONFIRMED MECHANICALLY: the 31 rows cycle indep:001..012 round-robin — the reuse
histogram is exactly 3,3,3,3,3,3,3,2,2,2,2,2. The legendary-action row cites
indep:005, whose canonical finding is spell-procedure completeness. The
spellbook-copy row cites indep:011, whose canonical finding is the
language-universe policy. The resolver accepts any alias from a hard-coded
universe, so relevance is never checked.
FIX:
 * commit an alias -> canonical finding SUBJECT table derived from
   /mnt/d/eshyra-2026-07-24-audit-repair-bead-plan.md (sections 'Independent Sol
   audit', 'Opus 5 original audit', 'Opus 5 amended...', 'GPT-5.6-Sol agent
   audit', 'Fable 5 audit');
 * each audit-finding evidence item must carry a per-row relevance statement
   tying that finding's subject to THAT primitive;
 * reject a relevance statement that is constant across rows or derivable from
   the primitive name by substitution — reuse the technique that worked for
   invariants in PR #476;
 * where NO audit finding genuinely supports a primitive, drop the audit-finding
   evidence for that row rather than inventing a citation. A row may stand on
   readiness/code/bead evidence alone.

=== F3: KNOWN-MISSING CLAUSES ARE NOT PROVEN ABSENT ===
sourceRef is 'SRD5.1:<primitive>' and locator is
'known-missing/<engine>/<primitive>' — both invented from the row's own name.
The resolver then searches the serialized pack for those invented markers.
Absence of a string you just made up proves nothing about the source procedure
or its projection. The regression test only proves an injected marker is
detectable.
FIX: a known-missing row must name a REAL source anchor (sourceRef plus a
locator that identifies actual SRD 5.1 material) and prove BOTH that the source
material exists at that anchor AND that no pack record or clause projects it.
If a real anchor cannot be supplied for a primitive right now, mark that row
with a machine-checkable 'evidence-underived' status that FAILS the closure
predicate, naming a follow-up bead. Do not keep a synthetic marker.

=== F4: owningBead IS NOT TIED TO BEAD EVIDENCE ===
owningBead is checked only for ID syntax; bead resolution runs on separate
evidence entries and equality is never required. Confirmed: 1 of 31 rows — the
spellbook-copy row naming eshyra-o9bd.19.5.5.3 — has no bead evidence for its
owner.
FIX: require that every 'owned' row's owningBead appears as a bead-evidence
entry on that row, and that the entry resolves. Test the mismatch case.

=== F5: SAME-ROW DUPLICATE QUERY BINDINGS ===
queryOwners maps queryId -> primitive, so the same queryId twice within ONE row
passes whenever the obligationIds differ. The test named for duplicate bindings
never constructs that case.
FIX: reject a queryId appearing twice in the same row, and add the missing test.

=== F6 (supervisor): obligationId VIOLATES THE SHARED CROSS-PR FORMAT ===
Observed: 'obl:::legendary-action-allowance-and-option-cost:missing-source-clause'
— the sourceRef and locator segments are EMPTY. The binding format fixed across
PRs #475/#476/#477 is obl:<sourceRef>:<locator>:<facet>.
FIX: validate the format structurally — four non-empty segments — and reject
empty segments. Correct every offending row. This is the identity #476 and #475
must join against later, so a malformed one silently breaks integration.

=== PRESERVE ===
Per-source evidence union with per-kind resolvers; exact structured hook
identity with its near-match negative tests; positive proof-of-absence
discipline; the umbrella-closure classification and .6/.7/.9/.12 routing;
proposed-row representability; the pinned seven non-pack primitives; recursive
stored-count rejection. Keep their tests.

The reviewer explicitly WITHDREW earlier objections: code evidence proving an
exported symbol exists is fine; bead checks may skip when bd is absent; this
bead need not execute full pack-driven engine scenarios. Do not 'fix' those.

=== ENVIRONMENT / CONSTRAINTS ===
npm ci first; npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. Edit only the four
files above. Do not touch package.json, internal.ts, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md,
.github/, or any script/CI file. Do not regenerate the pack or run the importer.
Do not modify any bead but your own; no bd dolt push; no push, PR comment, or
merge. Never delete a test to make a finding disappear.
acceptance_criteria:
• A canonical versioned primitive roster exists and the validator asserts exact set equality; missing and unexpected rows both fail, tested both ways.
• Audit-finding evidence carries a per-row relevance statement checked against a committed alias-to-subject table; constant or name-derived statements are rejected; unsupported citations are dropped rather than invented.
• Known-missing rows name a real source anchor and prove both source presence and pack absence, or carry evidence-underived status that fails the closure predicate.
• Every owned row owningBead appears as a resolving bead-evidence entry on that row; mismatch is tested.
• A queryId repeated within one row is rejected, with the missing test added.
• obligationId is structurally validated as four non-empty segments and every row conforms.
• All preserved behaviours and their tests remain; withdrawn objections are not re-litigated.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
notes: Completion report (commit 71d4eed): re-architected the bootstrap ledger around an exact versioned 31-entry primitive roster; added the canonical 2026-07-24 audit alias-to-subject registry and unique per-row relevance validation; replaced synthetic known-missing sentinels with real SRD source-record anchors plus explicit complete-projection absence queries; bound every owned row's owningBead to bead evidence; rejected same-row duplicate query IDs; and enforced four non-empty obl:::sourceRef:::locator:::semanticFacet segments. Updated the owned JSON/Markdown artifacts and regression tests, including missing/unexpected roster, relevance, real-anchor/projection, owner mismatch, duplicate query, and malformed identity cases.
